scene-u01.name: Pattern Recognition Week 3 KP04 Online Perceptron (expert-first, English)

p01-rule-title.name: p01-rule-title
p01-rule-title.text: Online perceptron: one sample at a time; correct only when wrong (or on the line)

p01-rule-ctx.name: p01-rule-ctx
p01-rule-ctx.text: Batch collects all wrong points, then changes once. Online flips one card at a time and decides at once.

p01-rule-src.name: p01-rule-src
p01-rule-src.text: Source: KP04 lecture §1.1 update rule; "$m\le0$ includes exactly on the line" follows the lecture's KP02 definition of needing correction.

p01-rule-c0.name: p01-rule-c0
p01-rule-c0.text: Every sample has only two outcomes. Look at the decision box: does it use the "current" $\mathbf v$ or the "updated" one?

p01-rule-ny.name: p01-rule-ny
p01-rule-ny.text: Yes: $\mathbf v\leftarrow\mathbf v+\rho\,y_i\mathbf a_i$ (positive adds, negative subtracts)

p01-rule-c1.name: p01-rule-c1
p01-rule-c1.text: "Yes": this sample is wrong, or exactly on the line ($m=0$), so correct. The correction uses this sample's own $\pm\mathbf a_i$ without waiting for others.

p01-rule-c2.name: p01-rule-c2
p01-rule-c2.text: "No": it is correct, so keep the weights. It still cost one inner product — correct does not mean zero work.

p01-rule-c3.name: p01-rule-c3
p01-rule-c3.text: $t$ counts "how many were presented", not "how many updates". A fixed data set must be presented over several passes before the finite-error guarantee for separable data applies.

p01-rule-c4.name: p01-rule-c4
p01-rule-c4.text: Difference from batch: batch uses one old $\mathbf v$ to find all wrong points, sums them and changes once; online looks at one and changes one, so the next one uses an already-new $\mathbf v$.

p02-trace-title.name: p02-trace-title
p02-trace-title.text: Original example: four points, v starts at 0, ρ=1, presented in the order A, B, C, D

p02-trace-ctx.name: p02-trace-ctx
p02-trace-ctx.text: A and B are positive (blue circles), C and D negative (red triangles). For each presentation see the score $g$, the labeled score $m$, the action and the new $\mathbf v$.

p02-trace-src.name: p02-trace-src
p02-trace-src.text: Source: KP04 lecture original Example 3.2; presentations 5–8 are a full re-check (lecture [correction]: the text says steps 5–7, which does not match a full pass).

p02-trace-c0.name: p02-trace-c0
p02-trace-c0.text: $\mathbf v_0=(0,0,0)$: all scores are 0; present A first.

p02-trace-c4.name: p02-trace-c4
p02-trace-c4.text: D: $g=-1$, $m=1>0$, correct, stays. End of the first pass: 2 updates, so we cannot stop yet.

p02-trace-c5.name: p02-trace-c5
p02-trace-c5.text: Second pass (presentations 5–8): scores $1,1,-1,-1$, all $m$ positive, no update. A full pass without updates: stop. Final $\mathbf v=(-1,1,0)$, boundary $-x_1+x_2=0$.

p03-effect-title.name: p03-effect-title
p03-effect-title.text: One update fixes the current sample; other points' scores change too

p03-effect-ctx.name: p03-effect-ctx
p03-effect-ctx.text: See how each point's labeled score $m=y\,\mathbf v^T\mathbf a$ changes under $\mathbf v_0$, $\mathbf v_1$ and $\mathbf v_3$. Green is $m>0$, red $m\le0$.

p03-effect-src.name: p03-effect-src
p03-effect-src.text: Source: Weights from KP04 lecture Example 3.2; each $m$ computed by build_kp04_en.py and checked by check_numbers_kp04.py; $m$ rises by $\rho\|\mathbf a\|^2$ (KP02 lecture).

p03-effect-c0.name: p03-effect-c0
p03-effect-c0.text: Start $\mathbf v_0=0$: all four points have $m=0$, all on the edge of needing correction. After updating A, what does each of the four $m$ become?

p03-effect-c1.name: p03-effect-c1
p03-effect-c1.text: Updating A: A's $m$ goes from $0$ to $2$ (an increase of $\rho\|\mathbf a_A\|^2=1\times2$). B is $1$; but C becomes $-1$ and D stays $0$: two points still need correction.

p03-effect-c2.name: p03-effect-c2
p03-effect-c2.text: Then updating C: C's $m$ goes from $-1$ to $1$. D has not been presented yet, yet its $m$ goes from $0$ to $1$: C's correction fixed D as well.

p03-effect-c3.name: p03-effect-c3
p03-effect-c3.text: An update only guarantees "this sample's $m$ rises by $\rho\|\mathbf a\|^2$". Others may improve (D) or get worse, which is why we present repeatedly and finish with a full re-check; one correct sample is not a reason to stop.

p04-stop-title.name: p04-stop-title
p04-stop-title.text: Predict: B is correct, can we stop? How far must we look before stopping?

p04-stop-ctx.name: p04-stop-ctx
p04-stop-ctx.text: Each of the eight presentations is a circle: orange = update, green = stay. At different positions we ask "can we stop now?".

p04-stop-src.name: p04-stop-src
p04-stop-src.text: Source: KP04 lecture §1.2 and "common myths": one correct sample is not a reason to stop; a pass with a correction in it is not either; stopping = a full pass with no update.

p04-stop-c0.name: p04-stop-c0
p04-stop-c0.text: Ask once at presentation 2 (B correct), presentation 4 (first pass done) and presentation 8 (second pass done): can we stop? Guess first.

p04-stop-c1.name: p04-stop-c1
p04-stop-c1.text: Presentation 2: B is correct, but that only means this sample has $m>0$. C after it is still wrong, so we cannot stop.

p04-stop-c2.name: p04-stop-c2
p04-stop-c2.text: Presentation 4: the pass is over, but this pass had $2$ updates. After updating, $\mathbf v$ changed, so earlier correct points must be checked again; we cannot stop.

p04-stop-c3.name: p04-stop-c3
p04-stop-c3.text: Presentations 5–8: check each of the four points again with the final $\mathbf v$; all stay. A full pass with no update is when we may stop.

p04-stop-c4.name: p04-stop-c4
p04-stop-c4.text: So "presentations" is 8 while "updates" is only 2. Stopping looks at "whether the last pass had an update"; if the data is not separable at all, this condition is never reached — the next KP deals with which weights to return in finite time.

p05-memory-title.name: p05-memory-title
p05-memory-title.text: What does online save? Must data sit in memory, or can it be read one at a time?

p05-memory-ctx.name: p05-memory-ctx
p05-memory-ctx.text: With $n$ samples of $d$ features each, compare "keep the whole batch at hand" with "keep only the current sample and $\mathbf v$".

p05-memory-src.name: p05-memory-src
p05-memory-src.text: Source: KP04 lecture §1.3: the online method's workspace is $O(d)$ (constant in the number of samples $n$); a full rescan still needs re-readable data; the speed advantage is not fixed.

p05-memory-c0.name: p05-memory-c0
p05-memory-c0.text: Batch handles all wrong points together; online handles one at a time. How much must each keep "at hand at the same time"?

p05-memory-c1.name: p05-memory-c1
p05-memory-c1.text: Workspace the online method needs: the weights $\mathbf v$ plus the current sample, size $O(d)$, not growing with the number of samples $n$. Data can be read in one sample at a time from disk or a stream.

p05-memory-c2.name: p05-memory-c2
p05-memory-c2.text: But a "full re-check pass" must read all samples again, so the data must be re-readable. For an ever-changing stream, the theorem's premise of a "fixed, separable training set" may not hold.

p05-memory-c3.name: p05-memory-c3
p05-memory-c3.text: Also do not misread: a correct sample still costs an inner product, so the computation does not become zero; online and batch usually take different paths, with no fixed speed ratio. What is saved is memory, not magic.

p06-practice-title.name: p06-practice-title
p06-practice-title.text: Practice: use the order B, A, D, C, start at v=0, ρ=1

p06-practice-ctx.name: p06-practice-ctx
p06-practice-ctx.text: Work it out first: score each sample with the "latest $\mathbf v$", then decide the action; in the end there must be a full pass with no update. Press Next when done.

p06-practice-src.name: p06-practice-src
p06-practice-src.text: Source: KP04 lecture practice; answer simulated by build_kp04_en.py (B update, A stay, D update, C stay, re-check), checked by check_numbers_kp04.py.

p06-practice-q.name: p06-practice-q
p06-practice-q.text: Order B, A, D, C. (a) The action at each presentation? (b) The final $\mathbf v$ and how many updates? (c) Is the boundary the same as in the original example? (Hint: what is D's score under $\mathbf v=(0,1,1)$?)

p06-practice-a1.name: p06-practice-a1
p06-practice-a1.text: (a) B: $g=0$, update $\mathbf v=(0,1,1)$; A: $g=1$ stays; D: $g=1$, $m=-1$, update; C: $g=-1$ stays.

p06-practice-a2.name: p06-practice-a2
p06-practice-a2.text: (b) Final $\mathbf v=(-1,1,0)$, $2$ updates; the re-check in presentations 5–8 all stay.

p06-practice-a3.name: p06-practice-a3
p06-practice-a3.text: (c) The update order differs and so do the intermediate $\mathbf v$, but this time we end at the same boundary $x_1=x_2$. In general it is not guaranteed; compute first, then compare.

p07-summary-title.name: p07-summary-title
p07-summary-title.text: Summary: one at a time, change only when wrong; stop when a pass has no change

p07-summary-ctx.name: p07-summary-ctx
p07-summary-ctx.text: Recall along the main example; the five conclusions of this KP are on the right.

p07-summary-e0.name: p07-summary-e0
p07-summary-e0.text: Rule: update $\mathbf v\leftarrow\mathbf v+\rho y\mathbf a$ only if $m=y\,\mathbf v^T\mathbf a\le0$, otherwise stay

p07-summary-e1.name: p07-summary-e1
p07-summary-e1.text: Trace: updates at presentations 1 and 3 of A, B, C, D; final $\mathbf v=(-1,1,0)$

p07-summary-e2.name: p07-summary-e2
p07-summary-e2.text: One update only guarantees the current sample ($m$ rises by $\rho\|\mathbf a\|^2$); other points change too

p07-summary-e3.name: p07-summary-e3
p07-summary-e3.text: Stop: a full pass with no update. 8 presentations, 2 updates; one correct sample, or a pass with updates, is no reason to stop

p07-summary-e4.name: p07-summary-e4
p07-summary-e4.text: Open question: for non-separable data this condition is never reached. Next KP: the neuron and the pocket algorithm
